claims.text: The investigated alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Slow cooling of this alloy produces several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases and a complex microstructure.
Rapid melt-spinning at approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s yields an amorphous structure in this alloy.
The rapidly quenched amorphous alloy remains susceptible to extensive primary crystallization during reheating.
Rapidly quenched material contains residual nucleation sites that trigger crystallization during reheating.
The relevant crystallization onsets span approximately 960 K to 1341 K.
A brief isothermal hold near 900 K is safely below the lower crystallization onset.
A post-quench isothermal hold near 900 K for seconds to a few minutes will structurally relax the amorphous matrix without causing significant crystallization.
Structural relaxation will reduce free volume in the amorphous matrix.
Structural relaxation will relieve quenched-in stresses in the amorphous matrix.
Reduced free volume and quenched-in stress will minimize nucleation sites for primary crystalline phases.
The brief hold permits short-range ordering and stress relief without long-range diffusion.
The hold will increase viscosity and thereby kinetically hinder nucleation and growth during subsequent reheating.
The annealed sample will retain a higher amorphous volume fraction than a rapid-quench-only sample.
The annealed sample will show delayed or suppressed crystallization exotherms relative to rapid-quench-only and slowly cooled samples.
Excessive hold time or temperature can initiate crystallization rather than improve amorphous retention.
